Definition: probably from the base of G2865; orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)):--adorning, world.
BiblicalUsage: Kosmos starts with the idea of order and arrangement, and in the New Testament it most often means the world as a whole: the created order, the people in it, and the system of life that runs apart from God. John 3:16 says God loved this world enough to give His Son, while 1 John 2:15 warns, "Love not the world", so the same word carries both God's love for people and the world's rebellion against Him. In 1 John 2:2 Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, and in 1 Corinthians 1:20 God makes foolish the wisdom of this world.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this world is both loved and lost: loved, because God gave His Son for it, and lost, because it has chosen its own way over His. My position is that a Christian lives in the world without belonging to its values, loving its people while refusing its rebellion.
RelatedTopics: Creation; Love of God; Salvation; Worldviews
